cues: For a telescope with a circular objective of diameter a, the first dark ring is at an angle one point two two lambda over a.
The factor one point two two comes from the circular shape.
So the smallest angle it can resolve is one point two two lambda over a, and its resolving power is the reciprocal, a over one point two two lambda.
A bigger objective resolves better, and gathers more light too.
That is why research telescopes have mirrors metres across.
